body:
The semantics of `WinScrolled` is "whenever the viewport changes". A buffer entering a window is a viewport change. This is so that plugins such as [nvim-treesitter-context](https://github.com/romgrk/nvim-treesitter-context) or maybe even treesitter highlighting can update visual content only for the current viewport. However it could be changed, because plugins could alternatively listen to both `WinScrolled` and `BufWinEnter`.

I can't reproduce the segfault with either test case, but I see why it happens. I'm not sure what would be the correct behavior for this case. Should it be disallowed? Or can freeing the window be deferred until the end of the iteration? What do `w_closing` and `b_locked` do?

Edit: meanwhile https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/13247/commits/0224d363bdf5ac0ae714b65a356c286557b7fc28 should prevent that from happening, but I worry that I haven't handled all repercussions of closing a window down the line.

issue.title: Fix & refactor autocommands

labels.name: needs:response
labels.description: waiting for reply from the author

repository.name: neovim
repository.description: Vim-fork focused on extensibility and usability

issue.body:
As discussed in #13117, some autocommands don't behave properly when called from outside the current buffer:
 - TextChanged,
 - CursorMoved
 - WinScrolled
 - BufModifiedSet (#13205)

The problem is that the check for wether or not to trigger the autocommand is always done inside either `normal_check` or `insert_check`. This means that when a plugin calls `nvim_xxx_set_xxx` from a non-current buffer, no autocommand is triggered. The code to check for those autocommands is also duplicated in those 2 check functions.

The goal of this PR is to separate checks for autocommands into well defined functions (`check_text_changed(...)`, `check_cursor_moved(...)`, etc) and those functions can be reused by both `normal_check` and `insert_check`, as well as any other place that might trigger those autocommands.

One open question that I have would be the correct behavior for triggering autocommands. The easiest way to do it would obviously be to fire the autocommand synchronously when the `nvim_xxx_set_xxx` function is called, OTOH it might be desirable to call it at another moment.

Tasks:
 - [x] Review all autocommands to find those behaving badly
 - [x] Refactor check functions for each autocommand
 - [x] Call those functions in relevant parts of the API
 - [ ] Verify if we want to restore window/buffers after autocommands

Related issues:
 - https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/10070
 - https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/13201

issue.title: Floating windows leak memory when there are folds

repository.name: neovim
repository.description: Vim-fork focused on extensibility and usability

issue.body:
Floating windows leak memory when there are folds. The example here is intended as a minimal reproducible example.

- `nvim --version`: `v0.5.0-dev+1115-gc1fbc2ddf`
- `vim -u DEFAULTS` (version: `8.1.2269`) behaves differently? Yes (when using popups in place of floating windows)
- Operating system/version: Ubuntu 20.04.2
- Terminal name/version: Konsole 19.12.3
- `$TERM`: xterm-256color

### Steps to reproduce using `nvim -u NORC`

```vim
$ nvim -u NORC
" Get Neovim's PID, which is used later for monitoring memory usage
:echom getpid()

" Create a new buffer
:let g:buf = nvim_create_buf(v:false, v:true)

" Set floating window options
:let g:opts = {
      \   'relative': 'editor',
      \   'width': 10,
      \   'height': 10,
      \   'col': 0,
      \   'row': 0,
      \   'style': 'minimal'
      \ }

" Define a function that opens a floating window then immediately closes it
:function! OpenCloseWindowHandler(timer) abort
:  let win = nvim_open_win(g:buf, 0, g:opts)
:  call nvim_win_close(win, v:true)
:endfunction

" Run that function every 10 milliseconds
:let timer = timer_start(10, 'OpenCloseWindowHandler', {'repeat': -1})
```

Next, monitor memory usage using Neovim's `PID` obtained earlier.

```
$ top -p <PID>
```

In the running Neovim, open a file and create folds. For example:

```vim
:help eval.txt
" Switching the `foldmethod` to `indent` will create many folds. They'll initially remain open.
:set foldmethod=indent

" WARN: Memory usage grows quickly. Closing the window with folds can be
" used to stop the experiment (halting the growth in memory usage).
:quit
" Alternatively, the timer can be stopped.
:call timer_stop(timer)
```

### Actual behaviour

Memory usage continuously grows when there is a buffer with folds while floating windows are opened and closed. In the example above, a gigabyte of memory is leaked in a few seconds.

Calling `garbagecollect()` at the end of `OpenCloseWindowHandler` does not prevent the memory leak.

### Expected behaviour

Memory usage remains bounded in this scenario.

### Additional information

The example above uses a timer since it's easy to trigger the leak this way. The timer is not what's causing the leak here, as similar results can be seen when using autocommands that trigger `OpenCloseWindowHandler`. For example, creating and deleting floating windows on `WinScrolled` events also results in a memory leak, but requires more work to reproduce (requiring scrolling through the document to trigger the events).

Update: The memory leak does not only occur for inherited folds, but also for newly created folds in the floating window. I've included an example in a [comment](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/14040#issuecomment-790109866) below.
